name: Yuqiao Liu
role: Data analytics · AI automation · Independent product development
summary: An Emory University MPH graduate in Biostatistics and a UC Santa Barbara graduate in Statistics and Data Science. My experience spans pharmaceutical commercial data, real-world evidence and clinical statistics. I also independently build and operate PinPet. I turn complex requirements into reproducible data workflows and usable products.

experience.text: Managed standardized monthly delivery of nationwide pharmaceutical commercial data and independently handled feedback and custom requirements for six pharmaceutical clients. Led a two-layer quality-control system combining LLM workflows with deterministic rules, automating approximately 80% of manual review work and reducing the recurring delivery cycle from five days to two.

Served as the independent statistician for a heart-failure study, covering the SAP, SAS propensity score matching, TLF and reports. Supported data processing for an observational prostate-cancer study and developed and reviewed patient funnel code for an early breast-cancer real-world study.

Cleaned and analyzed more than 12,000 electronic medical records with Python / pandas for two chronic-disease real-world studies. Translated clinical questions into analytical tasks and reviewed and reproduced statistical analysis plans and outputs.

projects.title: PinPet
projects.subtitle: Pet nutrition platform and domain-specific AI assistant development
projects.ownership: Independent product · Product strategy / UX / AI-assisted development / QA & operations
projects.intro: The recipe platform is live; an AI agent combining dog profiles, recipes and knowledge retrieval is in development.
projects.background: Pet owners need more than ingredient selection and a generated recipe: they need to understand nutrition results and turn saved recipes into meal plans they can follow. PinPet connects dog profiles, ingredients, calculated results and everyday planning, while exploring natural-language support for understanding individual recipes.
projects.goal: I independently own domain research, requirements definition, feature planning, UX, full-stack development, testing, deployment and maintenance. I am extending the live recipe platform with a domain-specific pet-nutrition AI agent and a RAG prototype.
projects.process:
Product strategy and end-to-end UX: Independently led domain research, requirements definition, feature planning and interaction design to address pet owners’ difficulties with ingredient selection, interpreting nutrition results and maintaining meal plans. Designed the full journey from dog profiles and ingredient selection to recipe generation, nutritional assessment, saved recipes and meal planning. Used ChatGPT to support frontend development and refined information hierarchy and user flows across desktop and mobile.

AI-assisted development and quality assurance: Used AI coding workflows for implementation, code review, test generation and automated backend log maintenance. Built the backend with Python/FastAPI and the frontend with React/TypeScript, with automated regression coverage for algorithms, APIs, frontend behavior and mobile user journeys.

Domain-specific AI agent and RAG design (in development): Designed a pet-nutrition assistant that combines dog profiles, selected recipes and conversational context to support nutrition Q&A, recipe explanations and ingredient substitutions. Structured nutrition research into knowledge cards with keywords, sources and review status, and built a keyword-based retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) prototype covering retrieval, context assembly and source attribution. Used Claude to support requirements decomposition, solution comparison and prompt iteration, translating domain knowledge into interactive product features.
projects.result: The live platform connects dog profiles, ingredient selection, recipe calculation, nutrient details, saved recipes and calendar plans. The AI agent and RAG prototype are in development, with knowledge cards still under review. A deterministic engine handles nutritional calculations; the LLM is separate from the calculation kernel. The screenshots below show the recipe platform, not a released agent. Scores illustrate software behavior under the current data and rules, not clinical validation or feeding recommendations.

projects.title: Bring review back to judgment
projects.subtitle: Sinohealth · Pharmaceutical data quality and review automation
projects.ownership: Sinohealth work case · Led quality-control system development
projects.intro: Flag exceptions with rules, organize evidence with AI, and keep adjustment decisions with the analyst.
projects.background: Monthly pharmaceutical data delivery involved repeated cleaning, anomaly checks and client-specific questions. Finding an unusual record was only the first step: analysts still needed to explain the signal and decide whether an adjustment was warranted.
projects.goal: I managed recurring data delivery and led development of a reusable QC workflow, separating deterministic checks, AI-assisted explanations and human decisions. The aim was to reduce repeated review work while keeping each adjustment traceable.
projects.process:
I organized anomaly flags, recent monthly values and review fields into a consistent workflow. Rules identify candidate records; an R/Shiny prototype lets analysts inspect them, request structured AI explanations and export the results to Excel. The prompt explicitly prevents AI from approving adjustments.

I also explored how to prioritize review using historical human labels. The archived experiment compares four model variants across a training month and a validation month, using precision–recall metrics, recall within the top-ranked records and estimated review volume. Missing human labels were treated as negative labels, which limits how the results can be interpreted.
projects.result: The archived materials include processing scripts, an AI explanation prototype, model comparison reports and review-list exports. In the two-month offline experiment, logistic regression ranked highest by PR-AUC. The model supports review prioritization; analysts retain the final adjustment decision.
projects.metrics: As stated in my résumé: approximately 80% of manual review work automated; recurring delivery reduced from 5 days to 2.

projects.title: Turning raw records into analysis-ready data
projects.subtitle: IQVIA · Real-world oncology studies
projects.ownership: IQVIA work case · Data processing / Programming / Review
projects.intro: Preparing data for analysis through record identification, mapping and code review.
projects.background: Real-world oncology analysis depends on how records are identified and classified, and how patients enter an analysis population. These transformations affect patient characterization and subsequent analysis.
projects.goal: For an observational prostate cancer study, I used SQL, regular expressions, mapping logic and systematic quality control. Separately, I developed and reviewed patient funnel code for a real-world early breast cancer study.
projects.process:
Prostate cancer: identification and mapping
I used SQL and regular expressions with mapping logic and systematic quality control to support patient characterization and downstream analytical decisions. The focus was to make identification and classification rules explicit in data processing and keep the outputs reviewable.

Early breast cancer: patient funnel
I developed and reviewed code implementing the study population selection logic. These were separate studies, presented here through their related data-processing responsibilities.
projects.result: Completed the relevant data-processing and patient-funnel programming and review work, supporting patient characterization and further analysis.
